newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes steady, ANS in question.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes steady, ANS in question.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes saw little activity Monday, suffering from a lull brought on by widely divergent views of the ANS market and the unexpected burst of buying in the outright NYMEX crude futures market.
Traders said there were no fresh deals to discuss, but the sellers of West Coast spot ANS placed the market at an offered range $1.75 below January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Bids were seen by the seller at a $1.95 discount to the WTI/Cushing. Buyers, however, said the ANS market was off the board, with no fresh deals seen due to the steep ask prices.
Jan WTI ended around $1.00 higher at $24.70-80 a barrel.
Traders said the $1.00 run-up in NYMEX crude made doing a deal for ANS even more uneconomical than last week.
"With that kind of rally I wouldn't want to do ANS at $2.50 under (the spot WTI/Cushing)," said one trader.

Fueling the outright price spike was the tightness in New York Harbor gasoline, thin volume and unsettled talk on the Iraq-United Nations oil-for-food deal. Most West Coast players were miffed by the crude rally, saying it pointed to nothing more than the need to deflate prices in the near-term.
"You tell me, there is supposedly Iraqi oil coming back to market this month and crude goes up like this," said a trader.
Other activity was muted, as Wilmington and Kern River were steady from last deals, traders said.
